pairs.fullEnglish: יַעֲקֹב lived in the land of מִצְרַיִם for seventeen years, and the days of יַעֲקֹב, the years of his life, were one hundred and forty-seven years.

The days of יִשְׂרָאֵל drew near for him to die. He called his son יוֹסֵף and said to him: If I have now found favor in your eyes, please place your hand beneath my thigh and deal with me in kindness and truth. Please do not bury me in מִצְרַיִם.
I shall lie down with my fathers; carry me from מִצְרַיִם and bury me in their burial place. He said: I shall do as you have spoken.
He said: Swear to me. He swore to him, and יִשְׂרָאֵל bowed at the head of the bed.
After these things, someone said to יוֹסֵף: Your father is lying ill. He took his two sons with him, מְנַשֶּׁה and אֶפְרָיִם.
Someone informed יַעֲקֹב, saying: Your son יוֹסֵף has come to you. יִשְׂרָאֵל gathered his strength and sat upon the bed.
יַעֲקֹב said to יוֹסֵף: אֵל שַׁדַּי was revealed to me at לוּז in the land of כְּנָעַן, and blessed me.
He said to me: I shall make you fruitful and increase you, and make you a congregation of tribes. I shall give this land to your children after you as an everlasting inheritance.
Now your two sons, who were born to you in the land of מִצְרַיִם before I came to you in מִצְרַיִם, are mine. אֶפְרַיִם and מְנַשֶּׁה shall be before me like רְאוּבֵן and שִׁמְעוֹן.
Your children whom you beget after them shall be yours. They shall be called by the names of their brothers in their inheritance.
יִשְׂרָאֵל saw the sons of יוֹסֵף and said: Who are these?
יוֹסֵף said to his father: They are my sons, whom יְיָ has given me here. He said: Please bring them near me, and I shall bless them.
The eyes of יִשְׂרָאֵל had grown heavy with old age, and he could not see. He brought them near him, and he kissed them and embraced them.
יִשְׂרָאֵל said to יוֹסֵף: I had not expected to see your face, and now יְיָ has shown me your children as well.
יוֹסֵף brought them out from before him and bowed with his face to the ground.
יוֹסֵף took both of them, אֶפְרַיִם in his right hand, to the left of יִשְׂרָאֵל, and מְנַשֶּׁה in his left hand, to the right of יִשְׂרָאֵל, and brought them near him.

יִשְׂרָאֵל stretched out his right hand and placed it upon the head of אֶפְרַיִם, who was the younger, and his left hand upon the head of מְנַשֶּׁה. He directed his hands wisely, for מְנַשֶּׁה was the firstborn.
He blessed יוֹסֵף and said: יְיָ, before Whom my fathers אַבְרָהָם and יִצְחָק served; יְיָ, Who has sustained me from my beginning until this day—

the angel who redeemed me from every evil—may he bless the youths. May my name be called upon them, and the names of my fathers אַבְרָהָם and יִצְחָק; and like the fish of the sea, may they multiply among human beings upon the earth.

יוֹסֵף saw that his father had placed his right hand upon the head of אֶפְרַיִם, and it was displeasing in his eyes. He supported his father’s hand to remove it from the head of אֶפְרַיִם and place it upon the head of מְנַשֶּׁה.
יוֹסֵף said to his father: Not so, my father, for this one is the firstborn. Place your right hand upon his head.

His father refused and said: I know, my son, I know. He too will become a people, and he too will increase. Nevertheless, his younger brother will increase more than he, and his children will be rulers among the peoples.
He blessed them that day, saying: Through you יִשְׂרָאֵל will bless, saying: May יְיָ make you like אֶפְרַיִם and like מְנַשֶּׁה. He placed אֶפְרַיִם before מְנַשֶּׁה.
יִשְׂרָאֵל said to יוֹסֵף: I am dying, but the Word of יְיָ will be your help and will return you to the land of your fathers.
I have given you one portion more than your brothers, which I took from the hand of the אֱמוֹרָאָה through my prayer and my supplication.
יַעֲקֹב called his sons and said: Gather together, and I shall tell you what will befall you at the end of days.
Gather together and listen, sons of יַעֲקֹב, and receive instruction from יִשְׂרָאֵל your father.
רְאוּבֵן, you are my firstborn, my strength and the beginning of my vigor. It was fitting for you to receive three portions: the birthright, the priesthood, and the kingship.
שִׁמְעוֹן and לֵוִי are brothers, mighty men. In the land of their sojourning they performed a mighty deed.
Cursed is their anger, for it is fierce, and their wrath, for it is harsh. I shall divide them in יַעֲקֹב and scatter them in יִשְׂרָאֵל.

יְהוּדָה, you acknowledged and were not ashamed; your brothers will acknowledge you. Your hand will prevail over your enemies; your foes will scatter and turn their backs before you. Your father’s sons will come forward to inquire after your welfare.

At the beginning there will be a ruler, and in the end a king will grow great from the house of יְהוּדָה. For from the judgment of killing, my son, you withdrew yourself. He will rest and dwell in strength like a lion and like a lioness, and there is no kingdom that will shake him.

One who exercises rule shall not depart from the house of יְהוּדָה, nor a scribe from his children’s children, forever, until the Messiah comes, to whom the kingship belongs; and the peoples will obey him.
His mountains will grow red with his vineyards; his wine-vats will drip with wine. His valleys will grow white with grain and with flocks of sheep.
זְבוּלֻן will dwell on the shore of the seas. He will subdue ports with ships and partake of the bounty of the sea; his boundary will reach to צִידוֹן.
יִשָּׂשׂכָר is wealthy in possessions, and his inheritance is between the boundaries.

He saw that the portion was good and that the land produced fruit. He will subdue the towns of the peoples and destroy their inhabitants; those who remain in them will be his servants and pay tribute.
From the house of דָּן a man will be chosen and arise. In his days his people will be redeemed, and in his years the tribes of יִשְׂרָאֵל will rest together.

The man who will be chosen and arise from the house of דָּן—his dread will fall upon the peoples, and his blow will prevail against the פְּלִשְׁתָּאֵי. Like a venomous serpent he will lie along the road, and like an adder he will lurk along the path. He will kill the mighty men of the camp of the פְּלִשְׁתָּאֵי, horsemen together with foot-soldiers; he will uproot horses and chariots and cast their riders backward.
For Your redemption I have hoped, יְיָ.
From the house of גָּד, a troop of armed men will cross the יַרְדְּנָא before their brothers for battle, and with many possessions they will return to their land.
The lot of נַפְתָּלִי will fall in a good land, and his inheritance will produce fruit for which people will give thanks and blessings.
My son who will increase is יוֹסֵף, my son who will be blessed like a vine planted by a spring of water. Two tribes will issue from his sons; they will receive a portion and an inheritance.
They embittered him, took vengeance upon him, and distressed him—mighty men, men of contention.

Your father’s blessings will be added to the blessings with which my fathers blessed me, which the great ones of old desired. May all these be upon the head of יוֹסֵף and upon the man set apart from his brothers.

בִּנְיָמִין—in his land the Divine Presence will dwell, and in his inheritance the sanctuary will be built. In the morning and toward evening the priests will offer the offering, and at evening time they will divide the remainder of their portions from the other sacred offerings.
All these are the twelve tribes of יִשְׂרָאֵל. This is what their father spoke to them, and he blessed them; each man according to his blessing he blessed them.
He commanded them and said to them: I am being gathered to my people. Bury me beside my fathers, in the cave that is in the field of עֶפְרוֹן the חִתָּאָה.
In the cave in the field of כָּפֶלְתָּא, which is opposite מַמְרֵא in the land of כְּנָעַן, the field that אַבְרָהָם bought from עֶפְרֹן the חִתָּאָה as a burial possession.
There they buried אַבְרָהָם and שָׂרָה his wife; there they buried יִצְחָק and רִבְקָה his wife, and there I buried לֵאָה.
The purchase of the field and the cave in it was from the children of the חִתָּאָה.
יַעֲקֹב finished commanding his sons, gathered his feet onto the bed, expired, and was gathered to his people.
יוֹסֵף fell upon his father’s face, wept over him, and kissed him.
יוֹסֵף commanded his servants, the physicians, to embalm his father, and the physicians embalmed יִשְׂרָאֵל.
Forty days were completed for him, for so the days of embalming were completed. The מִצְרָאֵי wept for him for seventy days.
The days of weeping for him passed, and יוֹסֵף spoke with the household of פַּרְעֹה, saying: If I have now found favor in your eyes, please speak before פַּרְעֹה, saying:

My father placed me under oath, saying: I am dying; in my grave, which I prepared for myself in the land of כְּנַעַן, there you shall bury me. Now, please let me go up and bury my father, and I shall return.
פַּרְעֹה said: Go up and bury your father, as he placed you under oath.
יוֹסֵף went up to bury his father, and all the servants of פַּרְעֹה, the elders of his household, and all the elders of the land of מִצְרַיִם went up with him.
Also the whole household of יוֹסֵף, his brothers, and his father’s household went. Only their little ones, their sheep, and their cattle did they leave in the land of גשֶׁן.
Both chariots and horsemen went up with him, and the company was very large.
They came to the threshing-floor site of אָטָד, on the far side of the יַרְדְּנָא, and there they lamented with a very great and strong lamentation. He observed seven days of mourning for his father.
His sons did for him just as he had commanded them.

His sons carried him to the land of כְּנַעַן and buried him in the cave of the field of כָּפֶלְתָּא, the field that אַבְרָהָם bought as a burial possession from עֶפְרֹן the חִתָּאָה, opposite מַמְרֵא.
יוֹסֵף returned to מִצְרַיִם—he, his brothers, and everyone who had gone up with him to bury his father—after he had buried his father.
They sent a command to יוֹסֵף, saying: Your father commanded before his death, saying:

Thus you shall say to יוֹסֵף: Please, now forgive the offense of your brothers and their sin, for they dealt evil to you. Now, please forgive the offense of the servants of your father’s God. יוֹסֵף wept when they spoke with him.
His brothers also went and fell before him and said: We are here as your servants.
יוֹסֵף said to them: Do not fear, for I am one who fears יְיָ.
You intended evil against me; from before יְיָ it was intended for good, in order to bring about what is seen this day: to keep a great people alive.
Now do not fear. I shall sustain you and your little ones. He comforted them and spoke words of consolation to their hearts.
יוֹסֵף dwelt in מִצְרַיִם, he and his father’s household; and יוֹסֵף lived one hundred and ten years.
יוֹסֵף saw third-generation children of אֶפְרַיִם. The children of מָכִיר, son of מְנַשֶּׁה, were also born, and יוֹסֵף brought them up.
יוֹסֵף said to his brothers: I am dying, but יְיָ will surely remember you and bring you up from this land to the land that He swore to אַבְרָהָם, to יִצְחָק, and to יַעֲקֹב.
יוֹסֵף made the children of יִשְׂרָאֵל swear, saying: יְיָ will surely remember you, and you shall bring my bones up from here.
יוֹסֵף died at the age of one hundred and ten years; they embalmed him and placed him in a coffin in מִצְרָיִם.

The כְנַעֲנָאָה inhabitants of the land saw the mourning at the threshing-floor site of אָטָד and said: This is a grievous mourning for the מִצְרָאֵי. Therefore its name was called אָבֵל מִצְרַיִם, which is on the far side of the יַרְדְּנָא.
The brothers of יוֹסֵף saw that their father had died and said: Perhaps יוֹסֵף will bear enmity toward us and indeed repay us for all the evil that we dealt him.
The days of דָוִד drew near for him to die, and he commanded his son שְׁלֹמֹה, saying:
I am going the way of all the earth. Strengthen yourself and be a man who fears sins.

Keep the charge of the Word of יְיָ your God: walk in ways that are right before Him, keeping His ordinances, His commandments, His judgments and His testimonies, as is written in the Torah of מֹשֶׁה, so that you may prosper in everything you do and wherever you turn.

So that יְיָ may establish His words which He spoke concerning me, saying: If your children guard their way, walking before Me in truth with all their heart and all their soul, there shall not cease for you a man upon the throne of the kingship of יִשְׂרָאֵל.
Act according to your wisdom, and do not bring his gray hair down in peace to the grave.
The mouth of the righteous pours forth wisdom, but the tongue of perverseness will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know what is pleasing, but the mouths of the wicked are perverse.
A deceitful measure is rejected by God, but His pleasure is in an upright weight.
As pride enters, disgrace enters; but wisdom is with those who are modest.
Falsehood does not profit on the day of wrath, but righteousness delivers from an evil death.
Show kindness to the sons of בַרְזִילַי the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they supplied my needs when I fled from before אַבְשָׁלוֹם your brother.

Here with you is שִׁמְעִי son of גֵרָא, a man from the tribe of בִּנְיָמִין, from עוּלֵימַת. He cursed me with bitter curses on the day I went to מַחֲנָיִם. He came down to meet me at the יַרְדְנָא, and I swore to him by the Word of יְיָ, saying: I will not kill you with the sword.
Now do not acquit him, for you are a wise man and know what to do to him. Bring his gray hair down to the grave by killing.
דָוִד lay down with his fathers and was buried in the city of דָוִד.
The righteous is rescued from distress, and an evil person enters in his place.
The days that דָוִד reigned over יִשְׂרָאֵל were forty years. In חֶבְרוֹן he reigned seven years, and in יְרוּשָׁלֵם he reigned thirty-three years.
שְׁלֹמֹה sat upon the throne of the kingship of his father דָוִד, and his kingship was firmly established.
אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ son of חֲגִית came to בַּת שֶׁבַע, the mother of שְׁלֹמֹה. She said: Is your coming in peace? He said: In peace.
He said: I have a word to speak with you. She said: Speak.
He said: You know that the kingship was mine, and all יִשְׂרָאֵל had turned their faces toward me to be king. But the kingship turned about and became my brother’s, for it was his from before יְיָ.
A deceitful person destroys his fellow with his mouth, but the righteous are rescued through their knowledge.
When it goes well for the righteous, their city rejoices; in the destruction of the wicked there is joy.
Through the blessing of the righteous, a city is exalted; through the mouths of the wicked, it is uprooted.
One who despises his fellow lacks understanding, but a man of discernment remains silent.
A slanderer reveals a secret, but one who is faithful in spirit conceals a matter.
Now I ask one request of you; do not turn me away. She said to him: Speak.
He said: Please speak to King שְׁלֹמֹה, for he will not turn you away, so that he may give me אֲבִישַׁג from שׁוּנֵם as a wife.
בַּת שֶׁבַע said: Good; I shall speak on your behalf before the king.

בַּת שֶׁבַע came before King שְׁלֹמֹה to speak with him concerning אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ. The king rose to meet her, bowed to her and sat upon his throne. He placed a throne for the king’s mother, and she sat at his right.
She said: I ask one small request of you; do not turn me away. The king said to her: Ask, my mother, for I will not turn you away.
She said: Let אֲבִישַׁג from שׁוּנֵם be given to אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ your brother as a wife.
Where there is no leader, a people falls; deliverance comes through an abundance of counsel.
A pious woman bestows honor, and the strong run after wealth.
A pious man repays good to his soul, but a cruel person destroys his body.
Thus one who does righteousness is kept for life, but one who pursues evil is kept for death.

King שְׁלֹמֹה answered his mother and said: Why do you ask for אֲבִישַׁג from שׁוּנֵם for אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ? Ask for him the kingship as well, since he is my older brother. Were not he, אֶבְיָתָר the priest and יוֹאָב son of צְרוּיָה in counsel together?
King שְׁלֹמֹה swore by the Word of יְיָ, saying: Thus may אֱלֹהִים do to me, and thus may He add, for אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ has spoken this word at the cost of his own life.
Now, as יְיָ lives, Who established me and seated me upon the throne of the kingship of my father דָוִד, and established kingship for me as He spoke: today אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ shall be killed.
King שְׁלֹמֹה sent by the hand of בְּנָיָהוּ son of יְהוֹיָדָע; he exercised power over him and killed him.

To אֶבְיָתָר the priest the king said: Go to עֲנָתוֹת, to your towns. You are a man liable to death, but I will not kill you this day, because you carried the ark of יְיָ אֱלֹהִים before my father דָוִד, and because you suffered in everything in which my father suffered.
God puts the crooked of heart far away, and takes pleasure in those who are blameless.
One who stretches out a hand against his fellow will not be acquitted of evil, but the offspring of the righteous is redeemed.
Gold rings in a sow’s nostrils—so is a woman who is beautiful but lacking discernment.
The desire of the righteous is for goodness, but the hope of the wicked is for wrath.
There is one who distributes and increases again; one who withholds from what is right has want.
An evil person does harm to a righteous person because he is surety for an outsider; and he hates those who place their hope in God.

qualifications.he: כינוי הוא והנושא המשתמע של ״ושונא״ נשמרים בתרגום ככינויים, בלי להוסיף זיהוי של אדם במקום שאינו מפורש. חילוני מתורגם כאן כזר, לא כשם של ציבור מודרני; המשפט אינו מובא כפסק מעשי על ערבות.
qualifications.en: The pronoun הוּא and the implicit subject of 'and hates' are retained as pronouns without supplying an identity not explicit in the wording. חִילוֹנַי is rendered as an outsider, not a modern community; the sentence is not presented as a practical ruling on guarantorship.
qualifications.anchor: בִּישָׁא מַבְאֵשׁ בְּצַדִיקָא מְטוּל דְהוּא עֲרַב חִילוֹנַי

pairs.fullEnglish: You also know what יוֹאָב son of צְרוּיָה did to me: what he did to the two commanders of the armies of יִשְׂרָאֵל, אַבְנֵר son of נֵר and עֲמָשָׂא son of יֶתֶר, whom he killed through his cunning. He supposed that their blood upon him would be reckoned to him like the blood of battle casualties, although he lay in ambush for them in time of peace. He shed their blood on the waist-garment at his loins and trod with the footwear on his feet.

qualifications.he: אספניקי מתורגם כאן בכינוי הכללי ״בגד מותניים״. אין בכך קביעה על גזרת הבגד, חומרו או אופן עשייתו, ואין הוא מוחלף אוטומטית בחגורה שבנוסח העברי.
qualifications.en: אַסְפְּנִיקֵי is rendered broadly as a waist-garment. This does not identify its cut, material or construction, or automatically replace it with the Hebrew text's belt.

pairs.fullEnglish: The wicked does a work of falsehood; one who sows for righteousness—his truth is his reward.
The righteousness of the blameless will straighten his ways, but the wicked falls through his wickedness.

qualifications.he: בנוסח המסופק תיאור התמימים הוא בלשון רבים, ואילו אורחתיה נושא כינוי יחיד. המעבר נשמר בתרגום; אין בו קביעה על זהותו של אדם נוסף.
qualifications.en: The supplied text describes the blameless in the plural but uses a singular suffix in אוֹרְחָתֵיהּ. The translation preserves this shift without identifying an additional person.

pairs.fullEnglish: My soul was not in their counsel; when they gathered to set out, I did not demean myself. For in their anger they committed slaughter, and of their own will they broke through an enemy’s wall.

qualifications.he: לִמְהַךְ נקשר כאן לשם הפעולה הסמוך בְּאִתְכַּנְּשֵׁהוֹן כתכלית ההתכנסות: 'כשנקהלו לצאת'. לָא נְחָתִית מִן יְקָרִי הוא משפט שלילה בגוף ראשון; הירידה מן הכבוד נמסרת כהשפלה עצמית, ולא כתנועה גופנית ממקום מסוים. אין תוספת של יעד או זיהוי מאורע. פירוש רש״י לעברית בדבר הזכרת שם האב בייחוס אינו מוכנס לדברי התרגום. בסוף נשמרים ההריגה וחומת האויב, בלי להחליפם בשור.
qualifications.en: לִמְהַךְ is attached here as purpose to the adjacent action noun בְּאִתְכַּנְּשֵׁהוֹן: 'when they gathered to set out.' לָא נְחָתִית מִן יְקָרִי is a first-person negative clause; descent from honor is rendered as self-abasement, not bodily movement from a specified place. No destination or historical episode is added. Rashi's Hebrew exposition about the father's name in a genealogy is not inserted into the Targum. The ending retains slaughter and an enemy's wall, not an ox.
qualifications.anchor: בְּאִתְכַּנְּשֵׁהוֹן לִמְהַךְ לָא נְחָתִית מִן יְקָרִי

pairs.fullEnglish: As for me, when I came from פַּדָּן, רָחֵל died to my sorrow in the land of כְּנַעַן, on the road, while a ploughing-distance of land still remained before coming to אֶפְרָת. I buried her there, on the road to אֶפְרָת, which is בֵּית לָחֶם.

qualifications.he: רש״י מפרש במפורש את תרגום אונקלוס: 'כְּרוּב אַרְעָא – כְּדֵי שִׁעוּר חֲרִישַׁת יוֹם', ומוסיף שהיה להם קצב שנקרא כדי מחרשה אחת. זה הבסיס למסירה הכללית 'מרחק חרישה'. לשון המקור כאן, כְּרוּבָא דְאַרְעָא, נשמרת בלי החלפתה בלשון שמצטט רש״י. אין כאן המרה ליחידות מרחק מודרניות או קביעה של מיקום הקבר; גם שיעור אלפיים אמה שבדיונו בפסוק העברי אינו מתווסף לתרגום.
qualifications.en: Rashi explicitly explains Onkelos's rendering, 'כְּרוּב אַרְעָא – כְּדֵי שִׁעוּר חֲרִישַׁת יוֹם', as the extent of a day's plowing, and adds that they had a fixed measure called a ploughing. This supports the broad rendering 'a ploughing-distance.' The supplied wording כְּרוּבָא דְאַרְעָא is retained, not replaced by Rashi's quotation. No modern distance conversion or grave location is established; the two-thousand-cubit measure in his discussion of the Hebrew is not added to the translation.

pairs.fullEnglish: His prophecy came true in them because he kept Torah in secret and placed his trust in divine might. Then gold would be placed upon his arms, and he inherited kingship and became strong. This came to him from before אֵל, the Mighty One of יַעֲקֹב, Who by His Word sustained fathers and children, the offspring of יִשְׂרָאֵל.

qualifications.he: הנבואה היא נושא המשפט, ובְּהוֹן מציין את מי שבהם היא מתממשת. ׳התגשמה בהם׳ מוסר את שיבת הנבואה כהתקיימות דבריה, לא כשיבת כוח הנבואה לאדם ולא כדימוי הקשת שבמקרא. רש״י מצטט כאן את לשון התרגום ומפרש ׳הַחֲלוֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר חָלַם לָהֶם׳. שמות או פרטי חלומות שלא נאמרו בנוסח אינם נוספים לגוף. הטעם עַל דְּקַיַּם אוֹרַיְתָא בְּסִתְרָא נשמר כטעם מפורש של התרגום.
qualifications.en: The prophecy is the subject, and בְּהוֹן identifies those in whom it is realized. ‘Came true in them’ renders the prophecy's return as the realization of its content, not as a person's recovering a prophetic faculty or as the Biblical bow image. Rashi explicitly quotes this Targum clause and explains הַחֲלוֹמוֹת אֲשֶׁר חָלַם לָהֶם, the dreams he dreamed concerning them. Names and dream details absent from the wording are not added to the body. The reason עַל דְּקַיַּם אוֹרַיְתָא בְּסִתְרָא is retained as the Targum's express explanation.

qualifications.he: רוֹחֲצָנֵיהּ הוא הביטחון שהניח, ובְתוּקְפָא הוא במה שנשען הביטחון: כוח או עוז. ׳עוז אלוהי׳ מבאר את זיקת העוז לאל על פי המשך הפסוק ועל פי דברי רש״י ׳אֵיתָנוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּבָּ״ה ... לְקֶשֶׁת וּלְמִבְטָח׳; אין זה תרגום של תּוּקְפָא כשם אישי ׳התקיף׳. בציטוט רש״י נמסר ׳וְשַׁוִּי תוּקְפָא רוֹחֲצָנֵהּ׳, ואילו הנוסח כאן משמר את הבי״ת של בְתוּקְפָא. לא אומצו ממנו אותיות חלופיות. הזהב מונח על זרועותיו בלי זיהוי מניחו ובלי הוספת טבעת, ופרנסת האבות והבנים מיוחסת במפורש למימרו של האל.
qualifications.en: רוֹחֲצָנֵיהּ is the confidence he placed, and בְתוּקְפָא identifies what it rests in: strength or might. ‘Divine might’ explains its relation to God from the verse's continuation and Rashi's אֵיתָנוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּבָּ״ה ... לְקֶשֶׁת וּלְמִבְטָח; it does not turn the abstract תּוּקְפָא into the personal title ‘the Mighty One.’ Rashi quotes וְשַׁוִּי תוּקְפָא רוֹחֲצָנֵהּ, whereas this source retains the ב in בְתוּקְפָא. No different source letters are adopted. Gold is placed upon his arms without identifying the placer or adding a ring, and the sustaining of fathers and children remains expressly through God's Word.

pairs.fullEnglish: The righteousness of the upright will rescue them, but plunderers are caught in their recompense.

qualifications.he: שִׁלוּם בניקוד שסופק הוא לשון תשלום וגמול, ולא צורת שְׁלָם במשמעות שלום או רווחה. לכן הצירוף מתורגם בגמולם. הכינוי מתייחס לבוזזים, ומִתְאַחֲדִין מציין את היותם נלכדים; לא נוסף גורם לוכד או משלם שאינו מפורש. אין כאן קביעה של סוג הגמול, זמנו או מסגרת כרונולוגית דתית, ואין שינוי בנוסח או בניקוד המקור.
qualifications.en: The supplied vocalized שִׁלוּם is the repayment or recompense word, not a שְׁלָם form meaning peace or wellbeing. The phrase is therefore rendered 'in their recompense.' The suffix refers to the plunderers, and מִתְאַחֲדִין expresses their being caught; no unexpressed captor or payer is added. The wording does not specify the kind or timing of the recompense or a religious chronology. The source wording and pointing are unchanged.

pairs.fullEnglish: When a wicked man dies, his hope perishes, and the hope of those who do wrongdoing will perish.

qualifications.he: עָאתָא מוסרת כאן עשיית עוול או מעשה רע, בלי לקבוע סוג מסוים של עבירה. אותה קבוצת אותיות חוזרת בפרק כא, פסוק טו, בצירוף דְעָבְדִין עָאְתָא, כנגד עשיית דין, ובפרק יט, פסוק כח, כתוכן היוצא מפי הרשעים. ההבדלים בניקוד נשארים כמות שהם; אין כאן החלפת הכתיב במילה אחרת. הצלע השנייה מדברת על העושים את המעשים האלה, ולא על בניו של הרשע.
qualifications.en: עָאתָא is rendered here as wrongdoing, without identifying a particular offense. The same letter sequence occurs at 21:15 in דְעָבְדִין עָאְתָא, contrasted with doing justice, and at 19:28 as what comes from the mouths of the wicked. The differences in pointing are left intact; no other spelling is substituted. The second clause concerns people who do these acts, not the wicked man's sons.

pairs.fullEnglish: יִשְׂרָאֵל will gather around his city; the people will build his sanctuary. The righteous will be all around him, and those who practice Torah will be with him in learning. His garments will be fine purple; his covering will be woolen cloth—woolen cloth dyed scarlet and in various colors.

qualifications.he: מֵילָא מוסרת כאן אריג צמר. בתרגום להושע ב, פסוקים ז ויא, היא באה בצירוף כְסוּת מֵילָא וּבוּץ, בתיאור כסות לצד בוץ. החזרה מֵילָא מֵילָא נשמרת גם בתרגום: הצמר נזכר, ושוב מתואר בצבעיו. אין מן החזרה לבדה קביעה של שתי שכבות, ואין כאן זיהוי של זן הצמר או שיטת האריגה. כינויי ׳עירו׳, ׳היכלו׳ ו׳כסותו׳ נשארים בלי להוסיף שם שאינו נאמר במשפט.
qualifications.en: מֵילָא is rendered here as woolen cloth. In the Targum to Hoshea 2:7 and 2:11 it occurs in כְסוּת מֵילָא וּבוּץ, describing clothing alongside fine linen. The repetition מֵילָא מֵילָא is also retained in English: the woolen cloth is named and then described again with its colors. Repetition alone does not specify two layers, and no wool variety or weaving method is identified. The referents of 'his city', 'his sanctuary' and 'his covering' are not given an added name absent from this sentence.

pairs.fullEnglish: Because you acted in accordance with your anger—behold, like water—but gained nothing, you shall receive no additional portion; for you went up to your father's bedchamber. Then you profaned my couch; my son, you went up.

qualifications.he: לָקֳבֵל מוסר כאן יחס של התאמה או היענות: הפעולה מתוארת כהיענות לכעסו של הנמען. אַפָּיךְ מובן בלשון כעס, ולא כקביעה על מיקום פניו. הביטוי הָא כְמַיָּא, ׳הנה, כמים׳, הוא השוואה קצרה שאין בה נושא או פועל מפורשים. היא יכולה להתייחס להתנהגות המתוארת או להציג את הנמען עצמו כמים; אין בה אמירה מפורשת שרץ, הציף או עשה מעשה נוסף. משום כך נשמרת באנגלית צורתה הקצרה של ההשוואה. בְּרִי שבסיום הוא פנייה ׳בני׳, והעלייה נשארת בגוף שני.
qualifications.en: לָקֳבֵל here conveys correspondence or response: the action is described as following the addressee's anger. אַפָּיךְ is understood idiomatically as anger, not as locating his face. הָא כְמַיָּא, ‘behold, like water,’ is a compressed comparison with no explicit subject or verb. It can refer to the conduct just described or present the addressee himself as like water; it does not explicitly say that he rushed, flooded anything, or performed an additional act. The English therefore retains the comparison's compressed form. The closing בְּרִי is the address ‘my son,’ and the ascent remains second person.

pairs.fullEnglish: The land of אָשֵׁר is good, and it produces royal delicacies.

qualifications.he: והיא מוסב על הארץ, המוציאה תפנוקי מלכים. והוא מרביא בתפנוקי מלכין הוא נוסח אחר; אין התרגום מתאר את אשר כמתפנק.
qualifications.en: והיא refers to the land, which produces royal delicacies. והוא מרביא בתפנוקי מלכין is a different reading; this English does not describe Asher as being pampered.

pairs.fullEnglish: The Word of the God of your father will be your help; and Sha"deye will bless you—with blessings descending from the dew of the heavens above, blessings flowing from the depths of the earth below, and the blessings of your father and your mother.

qualifications.he: ית נשמר במקור אך אינו נמסר במילה אנגלית נפרדת. הברכה נמסרת ״ושדי יברכך״; אין מוחקים מן המקור את המילה היתרה ואין מציגים פתרון דקדוקי ודאי לצירוף המקוצר.
qualifications.en: ית remains in the original without a separate English word. The blessing is rendered and Sha"deye will bless you; the additional source word is not deleted, and no certain grammatical resolution of the compressed construction is asserted.

pairs.fullEnglish: The wholeheartedness of the upright will guide them, but plunderers will be tossed about and crushed.

qualifications.he: תמימותא נמסרת כשלמות הלב ותמימות, ולא רק כיושר מוסרי מצומצם. לשון הבוזזים נשמרת כמות שהיא ואין משווים את נוסח התרגום מילה במילה לפסוק העברי.
qualifications.en: תמימותא is rendered as wholeheartedness and simplicity, not merely a narrower moral integrity. The plunderers clause is retained without forcing word-for-word agreement with the Hebrew verse.

dayTitle.he: צוואת הקבורה והביקור אצל האב החולה
dayTitle.en: The burial oath and the visit to an ailing father

explanation.he: יעקב מבקש מיוסף להוציאו ממצרים ולקברו בקבורת אבותיו, ומחזק את הבקשה בשבועה. בהמשך נודע ליוסף על מחלת אביו, והוא מביא אליו את שני בניו. הקטע מבחין בין בקשת הקבורה לבין הביקור הבא אחריה.
explanation.en: יַעֲקֹב asks יוֹסֵף to carry him from מִצְרַיִם for burial with his fathers and secures the request by an oath. Later, news of his father’s illness brings יוֹסֵף with his two sons. The burial request and the subsequent visit are distinct stages of the narrative.

dayTitle.he: הבטחת הארץ ומעמד שני בני יוסף
dayTitle.en: The promise of the land and the two sons of יוֹסֵף

explanation.he: יעקב מזכיר את ההתגלות בלוז ואת הבטחת הריבוי והארץ. הוא מונה את אפרים ומנשה לפניו כראובן ושמעון, ואילו הבנים שייוולדו אחריהם ייקראו בנחלתם על שם אחיהם. אין כאן הרחבה לדיני אימוץ או ירושה מחוץ לנאמר בקטע.
explanation.en: יַעֲקֹב recalls the revelation at לוּז and the promise of increase and land. He places אֶפְרַיִם and מְנַשֶּׁה before him like רְאוּבֵן and שִׁמְעוֹן, while later children are to be named under their brothers in their inheritance. This explanation does not extend the passage into a general rule of adoption or inheritance.

dayTitle.he: זכר קבורת רחל וקירוב הנכדים לברכה
dayTitle.en: Remembering רָחֵל and bringing the grandsons near

explanation.he: יעקב מזכיר את מיתת רחל בדרך ואת קבורתה בדרך אפרת. אחר כך הוא שואל לזהות בני יוסף ומבקש לקרבם אליו לברכה. לצד חולשת ראייתו בזקנתו נאמר שלא ציפה לראות את פני יוסף, וה׳ הראה לו גם את בניו.
explanation.en: יַעֲקֹב recalls the death and roadside burial of רָחֵל. He then asks who the sons of יוֹסֵף are and requests that they be brought near for blessing. Alongside the account of his impaired sight in old age, he says that he had not expected to see the face of יוֹסֵף and that יְיָ has shown him the children as well.

dayTitle.en: The deliberate placing of the hands and the blessing of the youths

explanation.he: יוסף מסדר את בניו לפי צדדי יעקב, אך יעקב מכוון את ידיו ומניח את ימינו על אפרים. הברכה מזכירה את עבודת האבות, את ההזנה עד היום ואת המלאך הפודה. בתרגום נאמר שהנערים ירבו כדגי הים בתוך בני האדם על הארץ.
explanation.en: יוֹסֵף positions his sons according to the sides of יַעֲקֹב, but יַעֲקֹב deliberately places his right hand on אֶפְרַיִם. The blessing speaks of the fathers’ service, sustenance until that day, and the redeeming angel. Onkelos explicitly compares the youths’ increase among humanity to the fish of the sea.

dayTitle.en: The precedence of אֶפְרַיִם and the promise of return

explanation.he: יעקב מסרב להחליף את סדר ידיו ומבחין בין עתיד שני האחים. הוא מבטיח שמימרא של ה׳ יהיה לעזר ושישיבם לארץ אבותיהם. החלק הנוסף ליוסף מתואר בתרגום כמי שנלקח בתפילה ובבקשה, ולא בחרב ובקשת.
explanation.en: יַעֲקֹב refuses to reverse his hands and distinguishes the futures of the two brothers. He speaks of the Word of יְיָ as their help and of their return to their fathers’ land. The additional portion for יוֹסֵף is described by Onkelos in terms of prayer and supplication, not the Hebrew verse’s sword and bow.

dayTitle.he: דברי יעקב לבניו כפי שהם מתפרשים בתרגום
dayTitle.en: The words to the sons as expounded in Onkelos

explanation.he: בני יעקב נקראים לשמוע על העתיד, והתרגום מרחיב את דימויי הפסוקים לתיאורי מלכות, נחלות, מלחמה ופרנסה. מלכות יהודה, מושיע מבית דן ושני השבטים היוצאים מיוסף נזכרים במפורש. משמעותן המדויקת של כמה מן הלשונות בדברי יעקב לראובן, לשמעון וללוי ובברכות יהודה ויוסף נותרת בלתי מוכרעת.
explanation.en: The sons are called to hear what lies ahead, and Onkelos expands the verses’ images into accounts of kingship, territory, warfare, and sustenance. The kingship of יְהוּדָה, a deliverer from the house of דָּן, and two tribes issuing from יוֹסֵף are explicit. The precise meaning of several expressions in the words to רְאוּבֵן, שִׁמְעוֹן, and לֵוִי and in the blessings of יְהוּדָה and יוֹסֵף remains unresolved.

dayTitle.he: ברכת בנימין, קבורת יעקב ופרידת יוסף
dayTitle.en: The blessing of בִּנְיָמִין, the burial, and the last words of יוֹסֵף

explanation.he: התרגום פותח בתיאור השראת השכינה והמקדש בנחלת בנימין, ולאחריו צוואת יעקב וקבורתו. אחר שובם למצרים חוששים האחים, ויוסף משיב שהוא ירא את ה׳ ומבטיח לפרנסם. בסיום הוא משביעם על העלאת עצמותיו וקושר זאת לזכירת ה׳ ולהעלאתם מן הארץ הזאת.
explanation.en: Onkelos first describes the Divine Presence and sanctuary in the inheritance of בִּנְיָמִין, followed by the burial instructions and burial of יַעֲקֹב. After the return to מִצְרַיִם, יוֹסֵף answers his brothers’ fear by saying that he fears יְיָ and will sustain them. His final oath concerns bringing up his bones when יְיָ remembers them and brings them out of that land.

dayTitle.en: David’s charge and keeping the Divine word

explanation.he: דוד מצווה את שלמה להתחזק ביראת החטא ולשמור את משמרת מימר ה׳. ההבטחה על המשך המלכות נמסרת עם תנאי של שמירת הדרך באמת. אחר כך נזכרים מעשי יואב וההוראה לנהוג בו בחכמה.
explanation.en: David charges Solomon to be strong in fear of sin and keep the charge of the Word of יְיָ. Continuance of kingship is stated with the condition of guarding the way in truth. The account then names יוֹאָב’s deeds and the instruction to act toward him with wisdom.

dayTitle.en: Wisdom, honest measure, and the guidance of integrity

explanation.he: פי הצדיק נובע חכמה ולשונו נבדלת מלשון ההפך. המידה והמשקל מדגישים את היושר מול המרמה, והגאווה ניצבת מול הצניעות. הסיום עוסק בהנהגת התמימים ובצדקה המצילה ממוות רע.
explanation.en: The righteous mouth pours forth wisdom, in contrast to a perverse tongue. Measure and weight distinguish uprightness from deceit, while pride is set against modesty. The ending concerns the guidance of the upright and righteousness delivering from an evil death.

dayTitle.he: חסד לבני ברזילי ודברי דוד על שמעי
dayTitle.en: Kindness to the sons of בַרְזִילַי and David’s words about שִׁמְעִי

explanation.he: החסד לבני ברזילי נקשר במפורש לאספקת צורכי דוד בבריחתו. דוד מזכיר גם את קללת שמעי ואת השבועה שנשבע לו במימר ה׳. לאחר הוראותיו נמסרת פטירתו וקבורתו בעיר דוד.
explanation.en: Kindness to the sons of בַרְזִילַי is explicitly connected with their supplying David’s needs during his flight. David also recalls שִׁמְעִי’s curse and the oath by the Word of יְיָ. His death and burial in the city of David follow the instructions.

dayTitle.en: Solomon’s established kingship and the coming of אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ

explanation.he: שנות מלכות דוד נזכרות לפי מקומן, ואחריהן מתוארת התחזקות מלכות שלמה. אדוניהו בא אל בת שבע וטוען שהמלוכה נטתה ממנו לאחיו. בדבריו הוא מייחס את המלכות שניתנה לאחיו למלפני ה׳.
explanation.en: David’s reign is stated according to its places, followed by Solomon’s firmly established kingship. אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ comes to בַּת שֶׁבַע and says that the kingship turned from him to his brother. In that speech he attributes his brother’s kingship to what came from before יְיָ.

dayTitle.he: דיבור החבר, שמחת העיר ושמירת הסוד
dayTitle.en: Speech concerning one’s fellow, the city’s joy, and keeping a secret

explanation.he: הדיבור הנכלולי משחית את החבר, ואילו דעת הצדיקים מצילה אותם. טובת הצדיקים וברכתם נקשרות לשמחת העיר ולהתרוממותה. בסיום נבדלים גילוי הסוד בידי מלשין וכיסוי הדבר בידי נאמן.
explanation.en: Deceitful speech destroys one’s fellow, while the righteous are rescued through knowledge. Their welfare and blessing are linked with the city’s joy and exaltation. The final sayings distinguish a slanderer revealing a secret from a faithful person concealing a matter.

dayTitle.he: בקשת אבישג והופעת בת שבע לפני המלך
dayTitle.en: The request for אֲבִישַׁג and בַּת שֶׁבַע before the king

explanation.he: אדוניהו מבקש מבת שבע לשאול את אבישג לו לאשה. בת שבע באה אל שלמה, והמלך קם לקראתה, משתחווה ומושיבה לימינו. לאחר רשותו לבקש היא מוסרת את הבקשה על אחיו.
explanation.en: אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ asks בַּת שֶׁבַע to request אֲבִישַׁג as his wife. She comes before Solomon, who rises to meet her, bows, and seats her at his right. After he permits the request, she states it concerning his brother.

dayTitle.he: תגובת שלמה והמשפט על אנשי המלכות
dayTitle.en: Solomon’s response and judgments concerning the royal figures

explanation.he: שלמה קושר את הבקשה למלוכה ומזכיר את עצת אדוניהו וחבריו. הוא נשבע במימר ה׳ ומוסר את ביצוע גזר הדין ביד בניהו. בדבריו לאביתר הוא מציין גם את החיוב וגם את הסיבות שלא להמיתו באותו יום.
explanation.en: Solomon connects the request with kingship and names the counsel of אֲדוֹנִיָהוּ and his associates. He swears by the Word of יְיָ and sends בְּנָיָהוּ to carry out the sentence. His words to אֶבְיָתָר state both liability and the reasons not to kill him that day.

dayTitle.en: Uprightness of heart, the hand’s act, and giving

explanation.he: הקטע מבחין בין עקומי הלב לתמימים ובין פגיעה בחבר לגאולת זרע הצדיקים. משל טבעות הזהב מדגיש יופי שאין עמו טעם. הסיום מעמיד את רצון הצדיקים מול תקוות הרשעים ואת המפזר מול החושך מן היושר.
explanation.en: The passage contrasts crooked hearts with the blameless, and an act against one’s fellow with the redemption of righteous offspring. The gold-ring comparison concerns beauty lacking discernment. The ending contrasts righteous desire with wicked hope, and distribution with withholding from what is right.

dayTitle.en: Leadership, surety, and the consequences of deeds

explanation.he: בהיעדר מנהיג העם נופל, והישועה באה בריבוי עצה. בהמשך נזכרים פגיעה בצדיק, ערבות ושנאה למי ששמים את תקוותם באלהים. אשה חסידה חולקת כבוד, חזקים רצים אחר עושר, והחסיד גומל טובה לנפשו. מעשה השקר עומד מול זריעת צדקה, והעושה צדקה נשמר לחיים מול רודף הרעה הנשמר למוות.
explanation.en: Without a leader the people falls, and deliverance comes through abundant counsel. The following saying mentions harm to a righteous person, surety, and hatred toward those who place their hope in God. A pious woman bestows honor, the strong run after wealth, and a pious person repays good to his soul. A work of falsehood contrasts with sowing righteousness, and one who does righteousness is kept for life while one who pursues evil is kept for death.

dayTitle.en: Righteousness, hope, and rescue from distress

explanation.he: צדקת התמימים מיישרת דרך, והרשע נופל ברשעו. צדקת הישרים מצילה אותם, ובמות הרשע אובדת תקוותו. הצדיק נחלץ מצרה, ואדם רע נכנס תחתיו.
explanation.en: The righteousness of the blameless straightens the way, while the wicked falls through his wickedness. The righteousness of the upright rescues them, and at the wicked person's death his hope perishes. The righteous person is rescued from distress, and an evil person enters in his place.
